[id="local-to-production-provider-swap-architecture_{context}"]
= Local-to-production provider swap architecture for LangGraph agents

[role="_abstract"]
You can deploy a LangGraph agent that you built and tested on your local machine to {productname-long} by changing provider configuration for inference, vector storage, and state providers, without modifying your application code.
The Llama Stack API serves as a standardized provider abstraction layer between your agent application and infrastructure services, routing requests to the appropriate backend provider based on configuration.

The agentic starter kits offer production-ready agent templates that use the Llama Stack API as a common interface.
By updating environment variables and Llama Stack configuration files, you swap local development providers for production services running on {productname-short}.
Your application code interacts only with the Llama Stack OpenAI-compatible API, so the same code runs unchanged in both environments.

== Provider abstraction layer

The Llama Stack API acts as a proxy between your LangGraph agent and the underlying infrastructure services.
In local development, you configure Llama Stack to route requests to lightweight providers such as Ollama for inference and Chroma for vector storage.
In production on {productname-short}, you reconfigure Llama Stack to route the same requests to enterprise-grade services such as vLLM or llm-d for inference and Milvus or PGVector for vector storage.

Because the API contract between your agent and Llama Stack remains the same, your application code does not change for inference, vector storage, and state providers.
Only the Llama Stack configuration and environment variables differ between environments.
Tool integration might require code changes to define Model Context Protocol (MCP) tool objects and pass them to the Responses API.
For more information about MCP tool integration, see xref:mcp-tool-integration-llama-stack_{context}[MCP tool integration with the Llama Stack tools API].

The following table shows how each agentic component maps from local development providers to production providers on {productname-short}.

.Provider mapping for local and production environments
[cols="1,1,1,1", options="header"]
|===
|Component
|Local provider
|Production provider
|Key environment variables

|Inference
|Ollama
|vLLM or llm-d via KServe InferenceService
|`INFERENCE_MODEL`, `LLAMA_STACK_SERVER_OPENAI`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`

|Vector storage
|Chroma or Milvus Lite
|Milvus or PGVector
|`MILVUS_URL`, `MILVUS_DB_PATH`

|State and memory
|SQLite or in-memory
|PostgreSQL. See xref:maintaining-agent-state-in-production[Maintain agent state and reliability in production].
|Configured in `run.yaml` under `providers.agents`

|Tools
|Local functions
|MCP servers: Kubernetes MCP Server, GitHub MCP Server
|`MCP_TOOL_MODEL`, `GIT_TOKEN`, `GITHUB_URL`

|Observability
|Local MLflow
|{productname-short} MLflow (planned -- not available in {vernum})
|`MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI`, `MLFLOW_EXPERIMENT_NAME` -- do not configure in {vernum}
|===

[NOTE]
====
MLflow-based observability and tracing for agentic applications is planned for a future release of {productname-short}.
Do not configure MLflow tracing environment variables for agent deployments in {productname-long} {vernum}.
====

== Configuration layers

The local-to-production migration involves four configuration layers.
Each layer controls a different aspect of the deployment.

`.env` file:: Specifies environment variables for inference endpoints, model identifiers, API keys, and MCP tool configuration. This file is the primary mechanism for switching between local and production providers.

`run.yaml`:: Defines the Llama Stack provider configuration. Each section, including `providers.inference`, `providers.vector_io`, `providers.agents`, `providers.tool_runtime`, and `providers.safety`, specifies which backend provider to use and how to connect to it. Environment variable substitution within `run.yaml` allows the same file to adapt to both environments.

Helm `values.yaml`:: Controls the Kubernetes deployment configuration, including the container image, resource limits, environment variable injection, and OpenShift route configuration. Per-agent value overrides customize the deployment for each agent variant.

Agent-specific configuration:: Defines agent behavior, including the LangGraph workflow, structured output schemas, and tool definitions. This configuration is part of your application code and does not change between environments.

== {productname-short}-managed and user-managed components

When deploying LangGraph agents on {productname-short}, some infrastructure components are managed by {productname-short} and some must be managed by the cluster administrator or the developer.

{productname-short}-managed components::
* Llama Stack operator and `LlamaStackDistribution` custom resource
* Model serving via KServe `InferenceService` with vLLM or llm-d runtime
* MLflow operator and tracking server (when enabled)

User-managed components::
* Vector storage services such as Milvus or PGVector
* PostgreSQL for agent state persistence
* MCP server deployments such as Kubernetes MCP Server and GitHub MCP Server
* Container image builds and registry management

[IMPORTANT]
====
The Helm chart provided by the agentic starter kits generates only `Deployment`, `Service`, `Route`, and `Secret` resources for your agent application.
The Llama Stack operator, `InferenceService`, and vector storage services are cluster prerequisites that must be configured separately before deploying your agent.
====

== Available agent templates

The agentic starter kits include the following LangGraph agent variants:

ReAct Agent:: A general-purpose agent that uses the ReAct pattern for reasoning and acting. Supports tool calling through MCP servers.

Agentic RAG:: An agent that combines Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) with agentic reasoning. Connects to vector storage for document retrieval.

ReAct with Database Memory:: A ReAct agent with persistent state backed by PostgreSQL. Maintains conversation history across sessions.

Human-in-the-Loop:: An agent that includes approval checkpoints for human review before executing certain actions.

Each variant uses the same Llama Stack provider abstraction and can be deployed using the shared Helm chart with per-agent value overrides.

[NOTE]
====
The agentic starter kits also include a LlamaIndex WebSearch Agent.
For information about LlamaIndex agents, see the link:https://github.com/red-hat-data-services/agentic-starter-kits/tree/main/agents[agentic starter kits repository].
====
